user_input: Implement the user's front-end dashboard redesign for mobile usability in this static HTML/CSS/JS expense tracker. Focus: mobile-first page; small compact overall dashboard values at top; category/subcategory spending prominent; below categories, a date-wise calendar/calendar-like month view with daily total expenses; below that transaction history. Keep desktop reasonably usable, preserve existing features (especially prior subcategory quick-add), ensure mobile layout usability. Read relevant project files; edit only frontend and related docs/tests if essential. Do NOT deploy or modify backend/IaC. Validate JavaScript and HTML/CSS as feasible. Report changed files and exact validation. Be bounded; do not make AWS operations.
title: Mobile Expense Dashboard Redesign

assessment_snapshot.intro: The project is a small expense tracker with a static frontend and separate Python backend:
bullets: The requested work is an in-place, mobile-first dashboard redesign with no stack change.
The desired dashboard order is compact summary values, prominent category/subcategory spending, daily totals in a calendar-like month view, then transaction history.
Existing behavior, especially subcategory quick-add, must be preserved; backend, infrastructure, deployment, and AWS operations are out of scope.

proposed_outcome: Redesign the existing static HTML/CSS/JavaScript dashboard for mobile usability while retaining the current stack, preserving existing expense-tracking features (including subcategory quick-add), keeping desktop reasonably usable, and validating the frontend without changing backend or infrastructure.
